title: Coefficient comparison for ordinary direct image
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $f\colon X\to Y$ is a $k$-morphism. The listed coefficient maps mean homomorphisms $A\to B$ of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$; $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ and $E\to F$ for finite extensions $F/E$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; $\mathcal O_E\to E$; $E\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; continuous homomorphisms $\mathcal O_E\to A$ to finite rings killed by powers of $\ell$; and finite composites of these maps. Here $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and $\mathcal O_E$ is its valuation ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]; the topological rings are regarded as condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with the filtered-colimit condensed convention for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Write $K_{\Lambda'}=\Lambda'_X\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}K$ for the derived coefficient change [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], and $\Dctf$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Use the derived module adjunctions of [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction].

For such a listed coefficient map $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ and $K\in\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ let
$$
\gamma_{f,K}\colon(Rf_*K)_{\Lambda'}\longrightarrow Rf_*f^*\bigl((Rf_*K)_{\Lambda'}\bigr)\simeq Rf_*\bigl((f^*Rf_*K)_{\Lambda'}\bigr)\xrightarrow{Rf_*((\epsilon_K)_{\Lambda'})}Rf_*(K_{\Lambda'})
$$
be the composite of the unit of $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ on $\D(-_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda')$, the
pullback identification of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1), and the extension of
scalars of the counit $\epsilon_K\colon f^*Rf_*K\to K$. Then:

1. $\gamma_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism for $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$; both sides lie in
   $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda')$.
2. $\gamma$ is natural in $K$, compatible with composition
   ($\gamma_{gf,K}=Rg_*(\gamma_{f,K})\circ\gamma_{g,Rf_*K}$ under $R(gf)_*=Rg_*Rf_*$), and
   compatible with the units and counits of $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ over $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$:
   writing $T_Z=(-)_{\Lambda'}$ and $c_f\colon f_{\Lambda'}^*T_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Xf_\Lambda^*$ for the inverse of the pullback identification, the unit and counit equations are
   $$\gamma_{f,f_\Lambda^*N}\circ T_Y(\eta_N)=Rf_{*,\Lambda'}(c_{f,N})\circ\eta'_{T_YN},$$
   $$\epsilon'_{T_XK}\circ f_{\Lambda'}^*(\gamma_{f,K})=T_X(\epsilon_K)\circ c_{f,Rf_{*,\Lambda}K}.$$
   These identities hold on the ambient derived categories wherever the displayed objects are defined.

proof.text: Cancel the structure morphism identities f.left ≫ Y.hom = X.hom to infer LocallyOfFiniteType f.left, QuasiCompact f.left and IsSeparated f.left. Use constructibleFiniteTor_stability_direct_images clause (3) at either admissible endpoint to obtain ordinary direct-image preservation. listedCoefficientCtf supplies endpoint admissibility and scalar preservation at both X and Y. Apply preservation in the two orders to get both outputs.

Obtain invertibility for the six primitive constructors and the algebraic-closure identity from scalarDirectImageElementaryCases. Induct on ListedCoefficientMap. In the composite a ≫ b case scalar preservation puts the intermediate scalar extension in Dctf, so both induction hypotheses apply. The coefficient-pasting equation of scalarDirectImageMateCoherence expresses scalarSixTower.hom followed by the composite mate as a composite of three isomorphisms: scalar change applied to the first mate, the second mate, and direct image applied to the source scalar tower. Cancel the invertible target scalar tower to get invertibility of the actual composite mate.

Use the naturality, geometric composition, unit and counit clauses of scalarDirectImageMateCoherence verbatim. For the clauses not involving geometric composition specialize its unused second morphism to the identity on Y. For geometric composition apply it to the arbitrary g : Y → W. These equations hold on the ambient derived categories and need no constructibility hypotheses.

source_error.place: Current blueprint direct-image proof, Finite rings paragraph invoking Stacks 0F12 on V and X_V.
source_error.failed_inference: Finite type over the arbitrary standing field does not imply finite absolute ell-cohomological dimension. Stacks 0F10(1) bounds the relative dimension of f; its absolute bound has an extra finite-cd(field) hypothesis, absent here. Thus applying the global-sections projection lemma 0F12 with an absolute bound is unjustified.
source_error.counterexample: For k = algebraic_closure(F_p)(t_1,t_2,...) and ell unequal to p, Kummer symbols in arbitrarily many variables survive successive variable-adic residue maps, so cd_ell(k) is infinite. Even V = Spec(k) is not bounded in absolute ell-cohomological dimension.
source_error.replacement: Keep the finite-ring projection-formula route, applying the existing relative projection lemma lem-sf-projection-finite-constant with the uniform relative bound from lem-kun-0f10(1). Its finitely presented constant module B need not be flat or have finite projective dimension.
